sam: Heads-up — I'm about to apply a Terraform change that adds a new mixed GPU node pool in us-west-2 with a small reserved capacity and spot fallback. Quick review + secrets wiring check pls. 

sam: TL;DR of the TF (will paste PR in a bit):
```hcl
resource "aws_eks_node_group" "gpu_mixed_pool" {
  cluster_name = var.cluster
  instance_types = ["p4de.24xlarge", "g5.12xlarge"]
  capacity_type = "SPOT"
  desired_size = 8
  min_size = 2
  max_size = 20
  tags = { role = "gpu-inference" }
}
```

sam: Plan is to reserve 4 instances via a small Dedicated pool (separate nodegroup) and let the mixed SPOT pool scale for burst. Need to confirm taints/tolerations and kubelet extra args.

mira: Can you confirm why p4de + g5 mix? latency-sensitive + cheaper burst? :thinking_face:

sam: Yep — p4de for low-latency heavy workloads, g5 for cheaper throughput. We'll route requests by model profile. Also want to use node taints so only inference pods land on GPUs: `node.kubernetes.io/gpu=reserved:NoSchedule` for dedicated ones, and `node.kubernetes.io/gpu=spot:PreferNoSchedule` for spot.

cheng: @sam do we have autoscaler config to prefer draining spot first on preempt? Also need graceful fallback to dedicated pool when spot capacity drops.

sam: Good call. Current plan: cluster-autoscaler on ASG tags with `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m` and node-group priorities set. I'll add a fallback policy in the routing layer: if model latency > 150ms for 3 consecutive mins, route to the dedicated model variant.

toni: For secrets: where are you storing the node bootstrap token and certs? We can't put AWS creds in TF state.

sam: Kept creds in Vault. Path: `secret/data/prod/gpu/nodepools` (KV v2). The TF uses the Vault provider to fetch the bootstrap key and writes a k8s secret via the kubernetes provider. Example snippet in the PR: 
```hcl
data "vault_kv_secret_v2" "gpu_bootstrap" {
  path = "prod/gpu/nodepools"
}
resource "kubernetes_secret" "gpu_bootstrap" {
  metadata { name = "gpu-bootstrap" namespace = "kube-system" }
  data = { token = base64encode(data.vault_kv_secret_v2.gpu_bootstrap.data.token) }
}
```

mira: We should use ExternalSecretsOperator (ESO) instead of writing secrets from TF. TF state can leak outputs even if coming from Vault. ESO will sync from Vault to k8s with proper RBAC.

sam: Good point — I can switch to ESO. That means TF will create the ExternalSecret CR instead of the k8s_secret resource. Will update.

cheng: Also update k8s toleration in the inference deployment: add `tolerations: - key: "node.kubernetes.io/gpu" operator: "Exists" effect: "NoSchedule"`. And ensure the daemonset that ships nv_peer_mem is on both nodegroups.

toni: For planning: make TF change in a feature branch, run plan with `-target=module.gpu` then create a small canary ng (2 nodes) in a staging cluster first. If staging is fine, apply to prod with `--parallelism=2`.

sam: Sounds good. I'll open the PR now, include the ESO CR example, autoscaler tag changes, and a short playbook for ops (how to promote reserved capacity).

infra-bot: deploy-preview: PR build passed (terraform fmt, validate, plan). Preview URL: https://ci.internal/reports/2061234567

mira: Quick checklist before merge: 1) ESO CR not exposing Vault token in TF outputs 2) Nodegroup IAM roles scoped to minimal permissions 3) ASG tag names matching cluster-autoscaler config 4) Runtime taint/toleration doc in repo.

sam: Adding checklist to PR comments. If no objections I plan to apply tomorrow 09:00 PDT and monitor for 30m. :thumbsup:

cheng: Ping me right before apply, I'll be on standby for draining operations.

toni: I'll coordinate with oncall to monitor GPU metrics and preempt rates.

sam: Thanks all — will post PR link in a min and mark as WIP until ES is wired.
